lines: Missed shots teach loudly, especially when everyone heard you brag first.
I once threw away a whole bundle because one shaft taught me suspicion.
There are nights when the bell rings and every arrow feels <shake>too few</shake>.
My first bowstring snapped so loudly that the golem turned around.
Once an arrow split another on the target and everyone became an expert immediately.
A child asked for an arrow that always finds home. I told them that is called a road.
During one raid, every arrow I had checked came back as a story instead.
I once chased loose feathers through the square while trying to look dignified.
A gust ruined a perfect shot and improved my humility.
The first bow I strung taught me to stand somewhere else before testing the second.
A trader bought hunting arrows and used them to hold up a tent.
One frozen morning the targets rang like bells.
I found a practice arrow in a fence post three days after losing it.
A golem stepped between me and the target once. I took the hint.
The best shot I ever saw happened after the archer stopped showing off.
A feather stuck to my sleeve all day and survived more work than most plans.
One practice session ended when a chicken claimed the range.
I saw fog swallow a target and make every archer suddenly philosophical.
An old bow here still creaks like it remembers the first raid.
I spent an afternoon tracking a missing arrow. A child had traded it for an apple.
